proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: After the storm took the power out for three days, the pump wouldn't restart. Bettina's crew found the control box had cooked, replaced it, and checked the pressure switch while they were there. Water back by supper.
reviews.name: Lorraine W.

reviews.text: Our water smelled like eggs in the shower for years. We thought that was just how it was out here. A test and a filter later, it doesn't.
reviews.name: Jerome A.

reviews.text: We built on a lot off a canopy road near Bradfordville and found an old well pipe in the woods. They sealed it properly and gave us the paperwork for the county.
reviews.name: Celia H.

reviews.text: Ditch water came over the wellhead during the flood. They shocked the well, waited, retested, and told us not to drink it until the second test came back clean. Patient people.
reviews.name: Wilson D.

reviews.text: New well for the farmhouse outside Havana. They talked us through where the limestone would likely start and why the casing has to sit in it. Good water, good pressure.
reviews.name: Margarite E.

reviews.text: Pump was twenty-some years old and finally quit. Quoted, scheduled, swapped, and they hauled the old one off. The orange stain on the tub is gone too.
reviews.name: Reggie K.

proof.guarantee: For 5 years after a storm or lightning strike, we recheck any pump control we installed at no charge.
